floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 8 confirmed; 8 diffs are TWO independent reg-alloc/scheduling ties (inner sum/j $a0 swap; 2nd-loop LICM-const vs move preheader order) — both pure-C, greg-characterized, frontier built.
Region A quantified as a pure sum/j $a0<->$a1 swap (all surroundings match target); naive structural levers KILLED, pointing to the directed permuter.

frontier.hypothesis: Directed permuter seeded from the floor-8 form sweeps the whole-function LUID cross-product that manual source order cannot reach, flipping the sum/j $a0 tie and/or the Region B const-vs-move order.
frontier.mechanism: The sum/j swap is a context-dependent local-alloc priority/birth-death tie (j 20000 > sum 13333) with identical surroundings; PERM_* over statement order in both regions + the range-check spelling explores the alloc/schedule cross-product. Vet any closing form against the cheat catalog (constant-holder / dead-store are the known traps here).
frontier.next_probe: Build clean single-fn target.o (asm/funcs/damage_DebugDisp.s + prelude, drop .set gp=64), seed base from candidate.c, run permuter_campaign with fresh-seed stopping rule; log to tmp/grind/damage_DebugDisp/sN/.

frontier.hypothesis: Lengthening j's live range past the loop (dropping j priority below sum's 13333) would flip Region A without touching bp.
frontier.mechanism: priority = log2(refs)*refs/range; j needs range>6 to fall under sum. Requires a genuine post-loop consumer of j's final value - none currently exists (offset+=0x24 is a literal in target; offset+=j either folds (no range extension) or changes the instruction).
frontier.next_probe: Search for a semantically-real post-loop use of the byte count; if none exists this axis is dead (offset+=j is a fold-or-diverge trap, not pursued).

frontier.hypothesis: A surrounding-code (outer-loop) structural change shifts the inner-loop birth/death LUIDs enough to lift sum above j while keeping bp highest.
frontier.mechanism: The tie is whole-function context-dependent; changing pseudo liveness in the outer loop / chkptr-offset handling could reorder the inner qty priorities.
frontier.next_probe: Perturb outer-loop tail / chkptr-offset derivation forms and dump greg qty_order for 77/78/79 each; keep only variants that hold score<=8 and move the order toward 78 77 79.
